_comment: Contrast CPU-bound vs IO-bound tasks. The two 'cpu_*' tasks each run 10ms then sleep only 100us — they want the CPU continuously and are good citizens for measuring throughput / fairness under contention. The two 'io_*' tasks run only 200us then sleep 2ms — they look like a network/disk-bound workload: short bursts of work interleaved with long blocking periods. A well-behaved scheduler should give the IO-bound tasks low wake-up latency (so their wake-respond-block cycle stays tight) without starving the CPU-bound tasks of forward progress. Run with --perfetto to compare wake-to-run latency for io_* vs run-time accumulated for cpu_*.
